plan: With 3 bidders and this ascending-clock structure (where each bidder exits at their sealed bid), the auction functions like a second-price auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid. Bidding my true value is the dominant strategy—it ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the price I'd pay, and never pay more than my value. Bidding above value risks losing money; bidding below risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $10.

Since this auction functions as a Vickrey (second-price) auction—my sealed bid sets my exit point, and I pay the second-highest bid if I win—the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if I win; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With a value of $30, bidding $30 maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids.

In this format, the sealed bid acts as my maximum willingness to pay in the ascending clock stage, and the auction effectively becomes a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid. The dominant strategy in a second-price auction is to bid exactly my true value, as this ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the price I'd pay, and never overpay. Bidding above or below my true value only risks either overpaying or losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid my true value of $25.
